title: The anchor account's van booked without its purchase-order number
purpose: Story S1. The fleet manager of company account A1 rings about a van with a check engine light. Maya asks good questions and takes the booking; she answers 'when can y'all look at it' with the opening hours, does not sum up, and opens the order without the purchase-order number the account's bills need.

call.day: the Wednesday of week T-17 (rule R6; card S01, call 23)

scenario.who_calls: Lonnie Coffey, fleet manager of company account A1, who rings the shop most weeks.
scenario.vehicle: unit ND-22, a 2020 Ram ProMaster 2500, BRC-4700 (accounts.json en.A1 fleet)
scenario.job: check engine light on, stumbling when it pulls away loaded: diagnose
scenario.wants: the van looked at as soon as possible
scenario.what_happens: Maya finds the unit by its tag, asks how it runs and whether the light is flashing, answers 'when can y'all look at it' with 'anytime', books the time he then names and says who checks it in. She does not ask for the purchase-order number and ends without a summary.

facts.note: Knowledge page 'Company accounts': A1's bills need its purchase-order number (card S01). No price is asked for on a fleet call like this one.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Maya, how can I help you?
Maya, it's Lonnie Coffey over at Nickajack.
Hey, Lonnie! How's it going?
Oh, it's goin'. I got — I got another one for you. Twenty-two's got a check engine light on, and the driver says it's runnin' rough.
Okay. Twenty-two... that's the ProMaster, tag ending four-seven-oh-oh?
That's it.
Okay. And — and rough like shaking at a stop, or more when he's getting on it?
He says it stumbles pullin' away from a stop. Loaded, mostly.
Okay. Is the light flashing, or just on?
Just on, far as I know. Came on yesterday.
Okay, good. Flashing would be a different story.
Yeah.
When can y'all look at it?
Oh, anytime! We're here seven-thirty to five-thirty, just have him bring it by.
Alright. I'll have him drop it first thing tomorrow, then, before his route.
Perfect. I've — I've got twenty-two down for tomorrow morning at seven-thirty, and I'll check it in myself.
He's gonna need it back quick as you can. I'm short a van as it is.
Okay, I'll tell the guys. I'll call you as soon as we know something.
'Preciate it, Maya.
Thanks, Lonnie! Talk to you then.
